Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
GOLD AND SILVER EMBROIDERY MATERIAL 

( First Revision ) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 31 May 1984, after the draft finahzed by the 
Precious Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural 
and Metals Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was earlier published in 1964. In the preseilt revision, a 
reference has been made to a comprehensive standard on methods of 
chemical analysis of gold and silver thread, 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*, The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of silver embroideries and 
gold coated silver embroideries, such as hadle^chalak^zik mlma^sadi^ tiki, 
l<angri. 

2. COMPOSITION 

2.1 The minimum silver content of the gold coated silver embroideries 
shall be 99' 5 percent by mass. The gold content of the gold coated silver 
embroideries shall be 0^5 percent by mass. The composition of gold and 
silver thread used in gold and silver embroidery materials should be as in 
tS : 2767-1984t and IS :3111-1984t. 

*Rules for rounding oil numerical values (tevhed), 
fSpccification for gold thread (silver hAsc){Jirf$ revismn)^ 
tSpccification for silver thrrad { first rtviston)* 

3 



IS : 3112 - 1984 

2.2 Purity of Silver — Silver used for the manufacture of silver embroide- 
ries shall be of 91*0 percent minimum purity as specified in IS :2U2- 
1981*. 



3. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

3.1 The wire used in embroideries shall be uniformly drawn and evenly 
coiled. The embroideries shall be of uniform thickness throughout. The 
gold coating shall be uniform and free from cracks and pores. They shall 
not show a tarnished appearance. They shall be compact and no space 
between consecutive spirals shall be visible. 

4. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

4.1 Lot — In any consignment, every 1 000 g or part thereof of the material 
shall constitute a separate lot. 

4.2 In order to determine the conformity of the lot to the requirements of 
this specification, a sample of 2 g shall be so selected as to be representa- 
tive of the lot. 

4.3 At least two chemical tests shall be carried out for each lot. 

4.4 The entire lot shall be rejected, if the sample representing the lot fails 
to meet the requirements specified in this standard. 

5. CHEMICAL ANALYSIS 

5.1 Gold and silver contents of the embroideries shall be determined in 
accordance with IS : 9925-19811. 

6. MARKING 

6.1 Each carton shall be suitably labelled with two labels, at the top and 
on one side of the lid. The labels shall bear the following information: 

a) Name or trade-mark of the manufacturer, 

b) Percentage of metals, 

c) Place of production, and 

d) Quantity (g). 



*Grad(.:s of silver and silver alloys ( first revision).

6.1.1 The labels after being affixed shall be coated with clear varnish to 
give a waterproof finish. 

6.1.2 The material may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

Note -The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. Th(^ISl Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply, with the requirements of that 
standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which 
is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer, ISI marked pro- 
ducts are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further 
safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for thr use of the ISI Certifica- 
tion Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, tnay be obtained from the 
luUiuu Standards Institution.
